chunks: Ali, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
My father (peace be upon him) said: 'No man strikes the Quran, part of it with the other, except that he disbelieves.'

key_terms.بَعْضَهُ بِبَعْضٍ: part of it with the other (referring to inter-textual interpretation or contradiction between verses)
key_terms.ضَرَبَ: to strike, to hit, or to compare/contrast (in the context of tafsir, to use one verse to explain or contradict another)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to 'strike the Quran part with part' and why does it lead to disbelief?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns against *ta'wil* (interpretation) that contradicts the clear text (*zahir*) or creates internal inconsistency within the Quran. It highlights the danger of subjective reasoning overriding the divine coherence of the scripture, a concept deeply rooted in the verse of *Mu'tashib* (3:7). This serves as a critical criterion for validating interpretive methods in Shia scholarship.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim Bin Suleyman, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No man would strike the Quran, part of it with the other (explain one Verse with the other), except that he would disbelieve’.
en.sarwar: 25. Ali has narrated from his father from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“My father has said, ‘Whoever mixes one part of the Holy Quran with the other part he turns into an unbeliever.’”
